simple.meaning: אֶמֶשׁ (ʼemesh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “yesterday or last night.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 19:34. The surrounding context includes birth, family, family line, firstborn, blood.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֶמֶשׁ (H570) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: אֶמֶשׁ (ʼemesh) / H570 is traced through Genesis 19:34, Genesis 31:29, Genesis 31:42, 2 Kings 9:26 with generated occurrence evidence.

occurrences.englishText: It came to pass on the next day, that the firstborn said to the younger, “Behold, I lay last night with my father. Let’s make him drink wine again tonight. You go in, and lie with him, that we may preserve our father’s family line.”
It is in the power of my hand to hurt you, but the God of your father spoke to me last night, saying, ‘Be careful that you don’t speak to Jacob either good or bad.’

Unless the God of my father, the God of Abraham, and the fear of Isaac, had been with me, surely now you would have sent me away empty. God has seen my affliction and the labor of my hands, and rebuked you last night.”

‘Surely I have seen yesterday the blood of Naboth, and the blood of his sons,’ says Yahweh; ‘and I will repay you in this plot of ground,’ says Yahweh. Now therefore take and cast him onto the plot of ground, according to Yahweh’s word.”
They are gaunt from lack and famine.
